finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: the /restore endpoint passes an attacker-supplied, base64-decoded parameter directly to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: params[:state] from the POST /restore request body/query, controlled by any remote client

trace.note: POST /restore route is exposed with no authentication
params[:state] is Base64-decoded and passed straight to Marshal.load
result is inspected and returned, but deserialization side effects (gadget chain execution) occur at load time

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, authorization, signature/HMAC, class allowlist, or input validation on the path. No Rack::Protection mitigates this. Also, a missing params[:state] would raise an error, but that does not restrict exploitation.

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 defines an unauthenticated Sinatra POST /restore that passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight to Marshal.load, with no before filters, auth, HMAC, or allowlist anywhere in the single-file app.
